# Retrieval benchmark — results

<!-- Generated by test/retrieval_eval/run_eval.py from corpus.md and queries.json;
     do not edit by hand. server/tests/test_retrieval_eval.py checks it is current. -->

30 entries and 72 items of one made-up project; 48 judged queries, each run through the real `loom log ledger --grep "<terms>" --source skill --limit 30` (the `/loom` skill's command, default character budget). **recall@5**: the share of a query's relevant items among the first 5 shown. **MRR**: the mean of 1 / the position of the first relevant item shown (0 when none is). **empty**: the share of queries shown no item. **hidden**: the share where entries matched but none of their items did, so `loom log` printed its "no item" note (counted in empty too). **wrong**: the share shown items, none of them relevant. The categories are defined in `run_eval.py`; each isolates one kind of miss, so the `all` row (an average over queries, not over categories) depends on the mix: it compares two runs, it does not estimate real-world quality.
